chunks: I asked al-Reza (peace be upon him), and I said to him: May I be sacrificed for you!
[Quran 16:43] 'Ask the People of the Reminder if you do not know.'

So he said: 'We are the Ahl al-Dhikr (People of the Reminder), and we are the ones to be asked.' I said: 'So you are the ones to be asked and we are the questioners?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Is it truly a duty upon us that we ask you?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Is it truly a duty upon you that you answer us?' He said: 'No. That is up to us — if we wish, we do so, and if we wish, we do not.'
Have you not heard the word of God, Blessed and Exalted: [38:39] 'This is Our gift — so bestow freely or withhold, without accountability'?

key_terms.أَهْلُ الذِّكْرِ: People of the Reminder — Quranic term (16:43, 21:7) reinterpreted in Shia tradition to refer specifically to the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt, not just scholars generally
key_terms.الْمَسْئُولُونَ: Those to be asked, those who bear responsibility for answering — the Imams as the authoritative source of Islamic knowledge
key_terms.عَطَاؤُنَا: Our Gift — in 38:39, referring to Solomon's divinely granted authority; the Imam applies this to the Imams' discretionary authority over imparting knowledge

ai.seo_question: Who are the Ahl al-Dhikr (People of the Reminder) according to Imam al-Reza in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: In this exchange, al-Washsha' quotes Quran 16:43 to Imam al-Reza (AS), asking about 'Ahl al-Dhikr' (People of the Reminder). The Imam confirms that the Imams of Ahl al-Bayt are the true 'People of the Reminder' whom God commands people to consult. The Imam further clarifies that while believers are obligated to seek guidance from the Imams, the Imams themselves exercise discretionary authority in answering, citing Quran 38:39 — a verse about Solomon's God-given authority to give or withhold — to establish that their disclosure of knowledge is a divine prerogative, not a compelled duty.
